English: I don't know **if** he's coming.
German: Ich weiß nicht, **ob** er kommt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: ob turns a yes/no question into part of a sentence; its verb goes to the end.

English: She's asking **whether** we have time.
German: Sie fragt, **ob** wir Zeit haben.
note — the bold part is what the card te: ob: whether. Never wenn here: wenn is for conditions and times.

English: Do you know if it **is going to rain** tomorrow? (one friend)
German: Weißt du, ob es morgen **regnet**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: The verb of the ob clause goes last: regnet.

English: I don't care **whether** it rains.
German: Es ist mir egal, **ob** es regnet.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Es ist mir egal, ob…: I don't mind whether…. mir is the dative.

English: I'm asking if you **can** help me. (one friend)
German: Ich frage, ob du mir helfen **kannst**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The modal goes last, after the infinitive.

English: Ask him if he **is coming along**! (one friend)
German: Frag ihn, ob er **mitkommt**!
note — the bold part is what the card te: At the end of the clause the separable verb is whole: mitkommt.

English: Do you know if she **studies**? (one friend)
German: Weißt du, ob sie **studiert**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: studieren: to study at university. Verbs in -ieren are regular.

English: Can you tell me where the station **is**? (formal)
German: Können Sie mir sagen, wo der Bahnhof **ist**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: The question word links the clauses, and the verb moves to the end. This is the polite way to ask.

English: Do you know when the train **leaves**? (formal)
German: Wissen Sie, wann der Zug **abfährt**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: At the end, abfahren is one word: abfährt.

English: I don't know what that **costs**.
German: Ich weiß nicht, was das **kostet**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: was … kostet: the verb last.

English: Can you tell me what the ticket **costs**? (formal)
German: Können Sie mir sagen, was die Fahrkarte **kostet**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: die Fahrkarte: the ticket for a bus or train.

English: He's asking how old I **am**.
German: Er fragt, wie alt ich **bin**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wie alt … bin: the verb last.

English: I have no idea where my key **is**.
German: Ich habe keine Ahnung, wo mein Schlüssel **ist**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: keine Ahnung: no idea.

English: Tell me why you **are laughing**! (one friend)
German: Sag mir, warum du **lachst**!
note — the bold part is what the card te: warum … lachst: the verb last.

English: Do you know who that **is**? (one friend)
German: Weißt du, wer das **ist**?
note — the bold part is what the card te: wer … ist: the verb last.

English: I'd like to know where you **live**. (formal)
German: Ich möchte wissen, wo Sie **wohnen**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wo Sie wohnen: the verb last.

English: I don't know what he **wants**.
German: Ich weiß nicht, was er **will**.
note — the bold part is what the card te: was er will: the verb last.

English: **When** I was a child, I lived in a village.
German: **Als** ich ein Kind war, habe ich in einem Dorf gewohnt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: als for one time or one stretch of time in the past. The verb goes to the end.

English: **When** I was little, we had a dog.
German: **Als** ich klein war, hatten wir einen Hund.
note — the bold part is what the card te: One period of the past: als. Then the main verb straight after the comma.

English: **When** we were in Berlin, it was cold.
German: **Als** wir in Berlin waren, war es kalt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: A single visit, so als.

English: **When** he was a student, he had no money.
German: **Als** er Student war, hatte er kein Geld.
note — the bold part is what the card te: als + war: one period of his life.

English: **When** she had a fever, she stayed at home.
German: **Als** sie Fieber hatte, ist sie zu Hause geblieben.
note — the bold part is what the card te: One occasion: als.

English: **When** I was a pupil, I sometimes didn't feel like it.
German: **Als** ich Schüler war, hatte ich manchmal keine Lust.
note — the bold part is what the card te: als for a time of life; manchmal: sometimes.

English: **When** I was a student, I lived with my parents.
German: **Als** ich Studentin war, habe ich bei meinen Eltern gewohnt.
note — the bold part is what the card te: als + one stretch of the past.

English: **When** we arrived, it was late.
German: **Als** wir angekommen sind, war es spät.
note — the bold part is what the card te: In a perfect at the end of the clause, the participle comes first and sind last.

English: When were you in Italy? (one friend) – **When** I was twenty.
German: Wann warst du in Italien? – **Als** ich zwanzig war.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wann asks the question; als answers it for the past.

English: I went to university **when** I was nineteen.
German: Ich bin zur Universität gegangen, **als** ich neunzehn war.
note — the bold part is what the card te: The als clause can also come second.

English: **Whenever** I was at my grandparents', we always went for a walk.
German: **Wenn** ich bei meinen Großeltern war, sind wir immer spazieren gegangen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: wenn in the past means whenever: something that happened again and again.

English: **Whenever** we had holidays, we always went to Italy.
German: **Wenn** wir Ferien hatten, sind wir immer nach Italien gefahren.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Every time, so wenn; immer makes the repetition clear.

English: **Whenever** it was Christmas, we always ate cake.
German: **Wenn** Weihnachten war, haben wir immer Kuchen gegessen.
note — the bold part is what the card te: Every Christmas, again and again: wenn.

English: We often went for walks **when** the weather was nice.
German: Wir sind oft spazieren gegangen, **wenn** das Wetter schön war.
note — the bold part is what the card te: oft: many times, so wenn, not als.
